mainText:
If you only remember one thing: the White House says top A I companies signed a self policing accord, while the labs themselves warn about self improving A I. Rules by promise, warnings from insiders.

Number one. A I models. From your Rundown: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet five point five. It nearly matches Opus five point five, at about half the price. It is also the first Sonnet with tougher cyber guardrails. Anthropic's developer conference also brought doubled rate limits, a big compute deal, and new agent features, including multi agent teamwork and agents that learn from past sessions. Open A I's Dev Day is today. Why it matters: the bar for Open A I just went up.

Number two. A I safety and policy. President Trump announced an accord, signed by leading A I companies, to self police A I development, after a White House tech lunch. Meanwhile, from your Rundown, Anthropic's Jack Clark, Open A I's Jakub Pachocki, Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio co wrote a paper urging preparation for an intelligence explosion. Anthropic says A I now does twenty six percent of its own research work, up from one percent in March. From Politico: benchmarks for chatbot mental health safety are becoming key for F D A approvals and kids safety rules. Why it matters: voluntary promises versus enforceable rules is the live fight.

Number three. Chips and geopolitics. Reporting says server maker Aivres, tied to blacklisted Chinese firm Inspur, shipped over five point six billion dollars of Nvidia chips to Southeast Asia, benefiting Chinese firms. Lawmakers are pushing two bills to close cloud access loopholes. Your Recode China newsletter says Meta's Muse agent has Chinese tech firms on high alert. Why it matters: export controls leak through cloud access and shell companies.

Number four. Deals. A M D agreed to buy Fei Fei Li's World Labs for eight point two billion dollars in stock. She becomes A M D's chief scientist. Meta launched an enterprise platform for its Muse models. Nvidia released an open blueprint to sandbox A I agents. And from The Information, investors are racing to fund on site power for data centers. Why it matters: compute and power are the bottleneck.

Number five. Tech for good. From Rest of World: the International Rescue Committee's Signpost program uses carefully tested A I agents in thirty countries, helping refugees and teachers, with humans handling the hard cases. Why it matters: in a crisis, reliability beats novelty.

Also in your Reads: The New Yorker on El Nino's weather chaos, and Galleries Now's week in art.

The thread today: power is concentrating in a few labs, and everyone is debating who checks them. Have a great day.
